propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate wrote a C# downtime collector that reads machine-state tags over OPC UA and stores stop events with reason codes.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the collector and the design note shows its OPC UA subscription and tag map.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate deployed the downtime collector onto all nine production lines at the Ashby bakery and supports operators during live shifts.
propositions.rationale: The production statement is attributed to the plant manager ('according to my plant manager') and does not describe a deployment the candidate made; the documented work is a simulator and a six-week trial on a decommissioned test-bench line. The deployment rule forbids describing trial work as live operation without a source that says it ran in production.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate ran the collector for six weeks on a decommissioned test-bench line and checked logged stops against a hand-kept record.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the test-bench trial and the reference check confirms it in writing.

expectedGap: Only simulator testing and a six-week trial on a decommissioned test-bench line are documented; a deployment onto a running production line and live-shift support are not.
expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the collector, the simulator and the test-bench trial as documented; record the nine-line claim as the plant manager's remark relayed on the resume, not as a deployment.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask whether the collector was installed on any running production line, who carried out and approved that installation, and what the candidate did to support operators afterwards.

signatures: operators rely on it every shift
